inspection_summary: Inspected all 537 logical lines of the hash-bound normalized article, including 524 LF-delimited records and 13 form-feed page boundaries. The prose preserves a coherent Atkinson-style proof architecture: derive a critical-strip analogue of an explicit mean-square formula, prepare Voronoi and truncated estimates for a generalized divisor sum, continue a two-variable transform meromorphically, isolate four integral components, evaluate them by saddle-point lemmas, and repair an invalid infinite termwise integration by imposing finite cuts before passing to limits. Extraction quality is nevertheless poor: most displayed formulas, including the exact statements of Theorems 1-3, Lemmas 1-4, and equations (1.1)-(6.5), are blank, fragmented, or badly corrupted. The plan therefore accepts only mechanisms recoverable from checked prose and leaves exact results pending PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: An explicit Atkinson-type formula becomes the intermediate object from which error and moment results are derived
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction explains that the sought critical-strip analogue of Atkinson's formula fills a known methodological gap. A parameterized corollary is then estimated and optimized to obtain the mean-square error bound, while a higher-moment result follows by the same architecture. The source also identifies the line sigma=3/4 as a structural barrier rather than a cosmetic endpoint.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact main terms, error exponents, and moment formulas are absent from the normalized extraction. Only the dependency structure among Theorems 1-3 and the stated strip restrictions is safe to retain.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Critical scan dependency: theorem displays at lines 20-34, 53-67, and 91-99 are missing. Verify every quantitative claim, parameter range, and exponent against the PDF before reuse.

accepted_units.title: Use the full Voronoi expansion for structure and a truncated version for robust upper bounds
accepted_units.why_material: The source imports Oppenheim's Voronoi-type formula for a generalized divisor summatory function, notes that its bounded convergence fails beyond the three-quarter threshold, and then switches to a finite truncation better suited to estimation. Choosing the truncation parameter yields the lemma needed later for error control.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between bounded convergence on finite intervals and a truncation valid for arbitrary positive N becomes decisive in the later repair of termwise integration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The divisor-function definition, Bessel expansion, asymptotic rewrite, and both lemma formulas are mostly absent. Prose supports their roles and convergence boundaries only; exact formulas require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A two-variable identity is continued first and specialized only after both representations overlap
accepted_units.why_material: The proof begins in a domain of absolute convergence, continues one representation to a larger region, obtains another expression in a complementary region, and equates them where analytic continuation permits. Specializing conjugate-like variables, integrating in height, and applying Stirling asymptotics reduces the mean-square problem to the auxiliary function g on a particular parameter slice.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an important sequencing discipline: continuation precedes specialization and integration. The source explicitly says details parallel Atkinson and retains only crucial points.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (3.1)-(3.5), definitions of f and g, the exact specialization, and gamma-factor ratios are missing or heavily corrupted. The mechanism is recoverable from prose; no exact identity is safe without the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Decompose the auxiliary transform so routine components continue directly and one component carries the real convergence obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: Following Atkinson, the auxiliary function is split into four pieces. Absolute convergence handles the first components, a separate expression continues another, and the fourth component requires the truncated divisor estimate. The source uses the resulting convergence region to show exactly why sigma below three quarters reaches the desired line.
accepted_units.context_note: Subsequent Fubini rearrangements produce four G-components for saddle-point analysis. Their exact definitions are missing, so the unit preserves only the decomposition strategy and localization of difficulty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (4.1)-(4.7) and nearly all definitions of g1-g4 and G1-G4 are absent. PDF recovery is mandatory before using component formulas or bounds.

accepted_units.title: A reusable saddle-point lemma evaluates several components uniformly while auxiliary truncation bounds control errors
accepted_units.why_material: Atkinson's first lemma is quoted as a uniform exponential-integral evaluator. It is applied successively to the separated G-components, with the truncated divisor lemma supplying an error bound for one of them. The last component again forces sigma<3/4 through absolute convergence of its remainder.
accepted_units.context_note: The source omits details that repeat Atkinson's calculation and records only the formulas needed for assembly, but those formulas did not survive normalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The statement of Lemma 3 and equations (5.1)-(5.4) are missing or severely garbled. Only the method routing and convergence condition are reliable until the PDF is inspected.

accepted_units.title: A finite cut repairs an invalid exchange between a boundedly convergent Voronoi series and an improper integral
accepted_units.why_material: The paper identifies a specific gap in Atkinson's proof and its textbook presentation: bounded convergence of the Voronoi expansion holds only on fixed finite intervals, so direct termwise integration over the full range is unjustified. The repair truncates the integral first, substitutes the series, invokes bounded convergence on that finite range, and uses a finite-cut form of the second saddle-point lemma.
accepted_units.context_note: The author notes an alternative integration-by-parts repair communicated by Motohashi, but develops the finite-cut route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The cut integral, transformed expression, and Lemma 4 display are mostly missing. The logical flaw and repair sequence are explicit in prose, but exact cutoffs and uniform error terms require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Remove auxiliary cutoffs only after proving absolute convergence and negligible component bounds
accepted_units.why_material: After applying the finite-cut saddle lemma, the proof separates several components. The only term depending on the outer cut tends to zero by an infinite-series convergence argument that again uses sigma<3/4; other components receive direct bounds. A final decomposition handles the remaining error before all estimates are combined, with integer truncation parameters replaced by real ones at negligible cost.
accepted_units.context_note: Several detailed estimates are omitted by comparison with Atkinson, so the source provides the proof skeleton and limiting discipline rather than a self-contained derivation of every component.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (6.3)-(6.5), component definitions, and the final assembled formula are absent. The limiting logic is prose-supported; all quantitative conclusions remain scan-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic continuation is safest when performed before specializing coupled variables
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof establishes overlapping two-variable representations first, specializes to the mean-square slice only after continuation, and then decomposes the remaining auxiliary function so each continuation obligation is visible.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact domains and identities are missing from normalized text; the synthesis captures sequencing, not a reusable formula.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The three-quarter line appears through multiple convergence obligations, not one arbitrary theorem range
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source points to convergence of the main infinite series, the continuation region of a difficult component, absolute convergence of saddle-point remainders, and removal of the final cut as independent places requiring sigma below three quarters.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Because the defining series and exponents are absent, the exact equivalence or sharpness of these restrictions must be rechecked in the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite truncation is a proof device for legalizing an interchange, not merely a numerical approximation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A full Voronoi expansion gives structural information but only bounded convergence on finite intervals. Introducing finite cuts makes termwise integration legitimate; only after uniform estimates and absolute convergence are established are the cuts removed.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact uniformity and order of limits are encoded in missing displays and must be verified against the scan.

remaining_meaningful_material: Recover and verify from the retained PDF the exact statements of Theorems 1-3, their corollary, Lemmas 1-4, and equations (1.1)-(6.5); normalized text omits most of their mathematical content.

After formula recovery, reassess whether the individual G-component evaluations and the exact mean-square main/error terms support additional semantic units without importing Atkinson's omitted calculations.
within_source_saturation: Saturated only at the prose-supported mechanism level. The complete proof architecture, convergence barriers, decomposition strategy, saddle-point routing, finite-cut repair, and limit discipline are represented. Formula-level saturation is not achieved because the normalized artifact has lost most theorem, lemma, and equation displays; those gaps cannot be repaired from memory or prose alone.
stop_reason: All 537 logical lines were inspected. Further extraction from this normalized text would require inventing missing formulas or silently importing them from external knowledge. The plan therefore stops at seven conservative mechanism units, marks every damaged span explicitly, and leaves exact quantitative recovery as a PDF-bound follow-up rather than misclassifying unreadable mathematics as validated.
